feedback.description: this memory records a correction somebody gave, and who gave it

memory.description: one thing a person said about how they want something built or handled, kept in their own words. The words themselves are the entity's doc.body, verbatim; these properties record where they belong and what is needed to read them. The byline is the entity's created{at, by}

space.description: whose space they were said in — every member of that space can read them, and they are deleted with it

about.description: the app they were said about, by slug, when they were about one

context.description: the line or two needed to understand the words — what was being talked about, never a restatement of what was said

memory_save.title: Save a memory
memory_save.description: Save what somebody said, in their own words. The memory is the sentence itself, never your summary of it, which can only hold less, plus a line or two of context somebody will need to read it weeks later. scope names the project it belongs to; leave it out when creating a principle that applies everywhere (when patching, omission keeps the existing scope). feedback names who gave the correction, when the words are one. Pass id to patch an existing memory instead of creating one: anything left out is unchanged, and replacing the words requires was, the string at $was.doc.body that memory_recall returns beside them, so a memory another writer changed since you read it is refused whole rather than overwritten. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Creating a memory requires nonempty said; omit id to create one.

said.description: the words the person used, as they used them

title.description: the index line a recall shows first

context.description: what was being discussed, in two lines; never a restatement of what was said

scope.description: project id or name; omit on creation for a memory that applies everywhere, or on a patch to keep the current scope

feedback.description: the correcting person’s id or name, or an empty string if unknown; either marks the memory as feedback

about.description: the app the words were said about, by slug

id.description: existing memory’s id or registered name to patch; omit to create a memory

was.description: the string at $was.doc.body on the memory returned by memory_recall; required when replacing existing words

memory_recall.title: Recall memories
memory_recall.description: Find saved memories containing all the words in said, not necessarily as an exact phrase. Pass words you expect the memory to contain, not a paraphrase. near is an entity id or name used to rank results by meaning when the server has a vector index for similarity search; it does not remove the said filter. Without near, results are newest first unless ids selects particular memories. With neither said nor near, returns the newest memories. Results are bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), including the full saved words and context, never snippets. Each carries $was.doc.body, the string to pass as memory_save’s was when replacing those words. Optional ids, scope and feedback narrow the results; limit defaults to 8.

said.description: words the memory must contain, matched as text terms rather than an exact phrase

near.description: entity id or name whose meaning ranks the results, when this server has a vector index; any said filter still applies

scope.description: project id or registered name; return only memories filed under it

feedback.description: only memories recording a correction somebody gave
